title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: The WSJ reported on Tue 17 Nov that Anthropic may price above $80 a share on strong demand, and Bloomberg reports investors were told the price will be at or above the top of the $70 to $78 range. Pricing is expected after the US close tonight, with first trade on Nasdaq as ANT on Thu 19 Nov; the final price and the first-day close are still open.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
next_label: Pricing tonight, first trade expected 19 Nov
sources: Anthropic, Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, CNBC, Yahoo Finance, TechCrunch

title: Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, Kress named interim
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: Nvidia reported Q3 revenue of $115.8B on Tue 17 Nov, above the roughly $108.7B consensus, and chair Harvey Jones said on the call that the board does not intend to reinstate Huang, CNBC and NBC News report. CNBC and Investing.com report the shares rose premarket on Wed 18 Nov and then turned lower, with neoclouds such as CoreWeave falling; the search for a permanent CEO is still open, and Bloomberg reports the board hired Heidrick & Struggles to run it.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
sources: Nvidia, CNBC, NBC News, Bloomberg, Investing.com, Yahoo Finance

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: ABC News and RTE report US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tue 17 Nov, and Gulf News reports Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait and on an Emirati tanker, which Saudi Arabia and the GCC condemned. Reuters reports Iran's navy said a fourth tanker caught fire within 24 hours after hitting a mine near Hormuz; the US blockade remains in place, and the indirect talks have produced no ceasefire.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: Reuters, ABC News, RTE, Gulf News, Khaleej Times, CoinDesk

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: Bitcoin Magazine reports Strategy fell below $100 on Tue 17 Nov as bitcoin dipped to about $63,300, and Investing.com reports the shares slid toward a $91.20 session low on Wed 18 Nov, with bitcoin near $64,000 against the roughly $75,452 average cost of its 850,849 BTC. The MSCI deletion takes effect after the close on 30 Nov; whether other index providers follow is still open.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, Investing.com, Bitcoin Magazine, Benzinga, 24/7 Wall St.
